comparison: Both strongly support the artificial selection experiment findings on lamina thickness increase (C1, C34-C38, C118). OpenEval provides detailed statistical and mechanistic support, while peer reviewers praised the directional selection approach and methodological correctness. Peer reviewers raised a minor concern about pseudo-replication in statistics that OpenEval did not address.

Both support optix's dual role in controlling pigment and structural color (C2, C46-C49, C97, C107). OpenEval emphasizes direct measurements and context-specificity with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers were enthusiastic about this finding, calling it 'of great interest' and appreciating the pigment-structure interaction emphasis.

Both support optix's context-dependent effects (C3, C50-C52, C54, C100). OpenEval documents context-specificity across scale types and wing regions. Peer Reviewer 1 explicitly praised this finding as 'interesting' and providing hints about developmental mechanisms, suggesting combinatorial inputs from positional information.

Both support comparative data across Junonia species (C41-C45, C92). OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance and consistency with thin film physics. Peer reviewers praised the 'impressive body of comparative data' and 'broad and sensible selection of specimens,' accepting the recapitulation of natural variation.

Both address lamina thickness-color relationships across species (C4, C55-C59, C61, C105, C108), but with different emphases. OpenEval finds strong statistical support following thin film physics. Peer Reviewer 2 expressed confusion about the thickness-color relationship direction ('seems in the wrong direction'), indicating unclear presentation despite accepting the underlying data.

Both support pigment-structure interactions (C62-C63, C67, C69-C71). OpenEval provides quantitative thresholds (0.2 AU) and empirical measurements. Peer Reviewer 2 specifically appreciated 'the emphasis on the interaction between structural and pigment colours,' indicating strong alignment.

Both support observations of pigment-structure interactions across species (C64-C66, C80-C81). OpenEval provides detailed absorbance and reflectance measurements. Peer reviewers accepted this as part of the comprehensive comparative analysis, with implicit support through praise of the 'broad selection of specimens.'

Both support claims about conserved lamina structure (C6-C7, C77-C79, C103-C104). OpenEval notes consistency across examined species with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers accepted these broader implications as part of their overall positive assessment, with Reviewer 3 noting the work represents 'an incremental advance' presented in 'a very convincing and comprehensive way.'

Both address Fresnel thin film modeling (C72-C76), but with different concerns. OpenEval supports the qualitative agreement while acknowledging quantitative discrepancies and blue-shift. Peer reviewers raised concerns about presentation problems (missing figure reference), systematic deviation causes, and notably the absence of empirical UV reflectance data (only model predictions), which Reviewer 3 called 'a great pity.'

Both address ground scale pigmentation changes (C116-C117, C128-C129). OpenEval supports findings with statistical analysis and functional interpretation. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted these observations as part of the artificial selection experiment, with Reviewer 2 appreciating the pigment-structure interaction emphasis.

Both address pigmentation changes in selection experiment (C128-C129). OpenEval provides statistical support with nested ANOVA and Mann-Whitney U tests. Peer reviewers accepted these detailed mechanistic findings as part of their overall positive assessment of the artificial selection work.

Both address detailed mechanisms in artificial selection (C112-C115, C119). OpenEval supports structural changes and pigmentation effects with converging evidence. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted these findings through their overall enthusiasm for the selection experiment and pigment-structure interactions.

Both address downstream mechanisms of optix (C102). OpenEval finds speculation reasonable and appropriately qualified. Peer Reviewer 1 explicitly requested more direct evidence, stating 'Any number of downstream genes might also influence lamina thickness' and that while optix is 'likely' responsible, 'this should be demonstrated/tested more directly.' This represents a significant divergence in confidence level.

Strong agreement on pigment-structure interaction examples across species (C135-C148). OpenEval provides detailed quantitative thresholds and measurements. Peer reviewers accepted these observations as part of the comprehensive comparative work, with Reviewer 2 specifically appreciating 'the emphasis on the interaction between structural and pigment colours.'

Both address optix mutant phenotypes (C130-C131). OpenEval supports observations and finds speculation about genotypic variation reasonable. Peer Reviewer 1's comment about optix being 'highly context dependent' directly references these varied regional effects, indicating acceptance.

Both address micro-macroevolutionary connections (C92). OpenEval supports the parallel between artificial selection and natural variation. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted this through their positive assessment of the comparative data showing recapitulation of natural variation.

Both address evolutionary scale connections (C108). OpenEval supports linking microevolution with macroevolution. Peer reviewers accepted this as part of the overall comparative framework, though Reviewer 2 expressed some confusion about the thickness-color relationship.

Both address future research directions (C101). OpenEval finds speculation about downstream mechanisms reasonable and appropriately qualified. Peer reviewers accepted the context-dependent nature of optix as 'interesting' and worth future exploration, indicating alignment on research directions.

Both reference butterfly vision (C76). OpenEval supports this claim through citation (Briscoe, 2008). Peer Reviewer 3 emphasized the biological relevance of UV reflectance and noted its absence from empirical measurements as 'a great pity,' indicating concern about missing data in this wavelength range.

OpenEval supports claims about color limitations of lamina structural colors (C82-C87) through theoretical physics and empirical observations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific claims about absent colors and brightness constraints.

OpenEval supports comparison to previous work (C89-C91, C150-C151) with quantitative differences and phylogenetic context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these comparative claims with Wasik et al. 2014.

OpenEval supports documentation of artificial selection timeline (C30-C33) despite acknowledging limitations in rigor. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing the experimental timeline documentation.

OpenEval supports background knowledge claims (C8-C29) about structural color physics and butterfly anatomy as established science. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these represent contextual background rather than novel findings.
OpenEval supports characterization of field state (C15-C17) based on cited literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing this literature review component.

OpenEval supports findings about brown scales having structural color (C39-C40, C122-C124) challenging assumptions about purely pigmentary brown coloration. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing this challenge to conventional assumptions.

OpenEval supports basic butterfly scale anatomy descriptions (C134, C152-C154) as established knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these represent anatomical context rather than novel findings.

OpenEval supports conclusion about system tractability (C109) as reasonable synthesis. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing this forward-looking conclusion, though peer enthusiasm for the system implicitly supports it.

OpenEval rates speculation about pigment placement function (C139) as uncertain due to lack of direct experimental evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing this hypothesis about pigment distribution effects.
